text:
Hi everyone. I’m desperately trying to figure out how to obtain a criminal background check and personal status certificate from Argentina for someone who was never a citizen or resident there.

I’m Israeli and my husband is American. I made Aliyah as a katin chozeret, and we are currently applying for his B/1 visa.

We gathered all of the required documents from the U.S., but PIBA then told us that because we spent significant time in Buenos Aires about 10 years ago, my husband also needs a criminal background check and personal status certificate from Argentina.

The problem is that we were never residents of Argentina. We went back and forth between Buenos Aires and the U.S. over several years, but we were always there as tourists. My husband never had a DNI, temporary or permanent residency, a work visa, or any other legal status there.

PIBA is not willing to waive the requirement.

I have contacted the Argentine Embassy, gone there in person, tried the official government websites, paid fees for applications that I could not complete because the system requires a DNI, and had a close friend in Argentina who is an attorney with the Justice Department visit government offices and try to help us. We keep getting sent from one office to another and have not been able to get the documents or even an official letter explaining that they cannot be issued.

We also have a pro bono attorney through the Jerusalem Institute of Justice, but her scope is limited to the Israeli side of the visa process, so obtaining the documents from Argentina is something we still have to solve ourselves.

We have now been given a final four-week extension. I am extremely stressed because this is the only thing holding up the application, and I honestly do not know what happens if we cannot get it done in time.

Has anyone dealt with anything similar, or does anyone have a contact in Argentina who understands how to obtain these documents for a foreign national who was only ever a tourist? An Argentine immigration attorney, government contact, document service, or any practical guidance would be incredibly helpful.

Thank you so much.
